svg.aria-label: Translation: the two TLBs and the walk
svg.text: Translation: the two TLBs and the walk
16 KiB pages and 48 bit virtual addresses. The set index bits are measured; the walk levels follow from the ARM 16 KiB granule; the cluster shared L2 TLB is a patent reading.
The virtual address as the TLBs and the walker slice it
derived from the ISA and the measured set bits
inferred from the ISA and patents
Latency ladder for a load, by where its translation and its data are found
cycles, with the confidence of each
page walk: three levels and a one bit level 0 at bit 47
L1 dTLB: set from VA 18:14, five bits, 32 sets of 5 ways is 160
L2 TLB: set from VA 21:14, eight bits, 256 sets of 12 ways is 3072
queued requests to the same page share it
user and kernel iTLB victims land here
loads never see the iTLB itself
Our probe for the single port
three loads a cycle to three pages
should fall to one per cycle
three loads to one page should keep three
the piggyback must carry most traffic
a size field is a patent reading
Shared by the cluster, beside the L2
cores keep small L1 TLBs, patent
the 25 cycles would include an L1 to L2 trip
a second core contends for it
two cores thrash their L1 dTLB, hit the L2 TLB
shared and single ported: per core cost rises
caches the upper two table levels
leaf entries read from the L2 cache
walk is one cache hit plus one L2 access
a load past a failed AUT is not performed
a page names one of 4 permission sets
switch a page with no shootdown
scan all entries or look up each page
ASID and VMID compared four at once
The iTLB shape does not fit
90 is a passing remark; 28 is 25 plus the 3 cycle hit
